name: Mount Kilimanjaro
headline: height
subtitle: Kibo summit, northeastern Tanzania
description: Kilimanjaro is a volcanic massif in northeastern Tanzania, close to the Kenyan border, and the highest point in Africa. Its central cone, Kibo, reaches 5,895 m (19,340 ft). The mountain stands on its own above the surrounding plains, and UNESCO describes it as the largest free-standing volcanic mass in the world.

measures.label: Height above sea level
measures.note: Summit of the central cone, Kibo; Britannica also gives 19,340 ft

measures.label: Rise above surrounding plains
measures.note: Height of the massif above the plains around it

facts.text: Kilimanjaro has three main volcanic peaks: Kibo, Mawenzi and Shira.
Kilimanjaro National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, covers some 75,575 hectares and is encircled by mountain forest.
Europeans first learned of the mountain in 1848, when it was reached by the German missionaries Johannes Rebmann and Johann Ludwig Krapf.

caveats: The Tanzania National Parks page for Kilimanjaro returned a 'page not found' error, so the height comes from Britannica and UNESCO, which agree on 5,895 m.
The 4,877 m rise is measured from the surrounding plains, not from sea level, so it is smaller than the summit elevation.
The mountain outline is illustrative; only its height above sea level is to scale.
